_lisezmoi: Taxe de vente des États sur l'or et l'argent d'investissement, relue État par État sur le statut officiel cité (curl, 2026-11-13). Un État absent n'a pas été relu : le site ne dit rien de lui. Écartés après lecture : Virginie (exonération § 58.1-609.1(19) « effective through June 30, 2025 », suite non relue), Washington (RCW 82.04.062 abrogé au 1er janvier 2026, régime nouveau non relu). rule : exempt (exonéré quel que soit le montant), threshold (exonéré à partir de `threshold` $ ; thresholdInclusive=false : il faut dépasser le seuil). Aucun taux n'est donné : il dépend de l'État et de la commune.

states.name: Arizona
states.scope: Precious metal bullion and monetized bullion (legal tender coins) are exempt; coins sold to be made into jewelry or art are taxed.

states.name: Connecticut
states.scope: Gold or silver bullion, gold or silver legal tender and rare or antique coins are exempt, except in a sale where the total value is less than $1,000.

states.name: Florida
states.scope: The sale of gold, silver or platinum bullion, or any combination of them, in a single transaction is exempt; coins are not named in this paragraph.

states.name: Iowa
states.scope: Coins, currency and bullion are exempt: bars, ingots or commemorative medallions valued for their metal, and coins that are or were legal tender.

states.name: Kansas
states.scope: All sales of gold or silver coins, and of gold, silver, platinum or palladium bullion (bars, ingots, commemorative medallions valued for their metal), are exempt.

states.name: Maryland
states.scope: Refined precious metal bullion and coins that are or were money are exempt when the sale price is greater than $1,000; jewelry and works of art are excluded.

states.name: Minnesota
states.scope: Bars or rounds of 99.9% or more gold, silver, platinum or palladium, marked with weight, purity and content, are exempt; jewelry, art and scrap are not.

states.name: Missouri
states.scope: Bullion of at least 900 parts per 1,000 and investment coins are exempt from state and local sales tax.

states.name: New York
states.scope: Bars, ingots or coins sold for investment are exempt when sold for more than $1,000, kept in the same form, and priced on their metal: coins at no more than 140% (silver) or 120% (gold of a quarter ounce or less) of metal value.

states.name: North Dakota
states.scope: Legal tender coins and currency, and precious metal bullion refined to at least 999 parts per 1,000 and valued for its metal, are exempt.

states.name: South Carolina
states.scope: Gold, silver or platinum bullion, coins that are or were legal tender, and currency are exempt; retailers keep a record of each exempt sale.
